study type: Pooled analysis of multiple prospective cohort studies with meta-analysis
cohort: The study included up to 24,861 mother-child pairs from 7 European mother-offspring cohorts.
finding: Higher maternal dietary quality (DASH score) was associated with higher birth weight, head circumference, longer birth length, and lower risk of LBW and SGA; conversely, a more pro-inflammatory maternal diet (E-DII score) was associated with lower birth weight, shorter birth length, and higher risk of SGA.
